_provenance: KILLROYWASHERE - VA Claims Assistant, created by EhrenAL
_note: Plain-language exam (C&P / DBQ) guidance by body system. Facts only; never coaching to exaggerate. Families are picked by diagnostic code (dc ranges) or words in the condition name.

before: Read your statement for this condition again, so the dates and examples are fresh.
Fill in your symptom log for a few weeks before the exam if you can.
Write down your 3 worst days in the last few months: what happened, how long it lasted, what you couldn't do.
bring: Photo ID and your exam appointment letter.
This prep sheet and your statement.
A list of your medicines, with how often you take each.
Any device you use (brace, cane, CPAP mask) and the prescription if you have it.
during: Describe your typical days AND your bad days. The exam can only record what you tell the examiner and what they see that day.
Be honest and specific: how often, how long, what you can't do. Don't downplay, and don't exaggerate.
If something hurts, say so right when it starts. Don't push through pain to look tough.
If the examiner doesn't ask about something important on this sheet, it's fine to bring it up.
It's okay to say 'I don't know' or 'I'm not sure'.
after: Write down what was measured and anything that seemed wrong (for example, the wrong body part, or a symptom left out).
You can get a copy of the exam report later. If it has a mistake, tell your VSO; it may matter for your rating.

joint.label: Joints (knee, hip, ankle, shoulder, elbow, wrist)
joint.measured: Range of motion with a measuring tool, motion after 3 repeats, pain, strength, stability, and the effect of flare-ups and repeated use.
tell: Where in each movement the pain starts. Stop there and say so.

How often you have flare-ups, how long they last, and how much less you can move or do during one. The examiner should estimate your motion during a flare-up from your description, even if you are not having one that day.
Whether the joint gives way, locks, catches, or swells, and how often.
Any brace, cane, or other device a provider prescribed, and when you use it.
Surgeries, and what is still wrong after them.

spine.label: Back and neck
spine.measured: Range of motion (bending forward, back, to each side, turning), pain, spasm, guarding, nerve symptoms, and the effect of flare-ups.
tell: How far you can bend on a bad day, and what stops you.
Flare-ups: how often, how long, what sets them off, what you can't do.
Pain, numbness, or tingling going into your arms or legs, and exactly where.
Any bed rest a doctor ordered in the last 12 months (dates and how long).
Bowel or bladder problems, if any.

muscle.label: Muscle injuries
muscle.measured: The cardinal signs of muscle injury: loss of power, weakness, lowered fatigue threshold, fatigue-pain, impaired coordination, and uncertainty of movement; also atrophy, scars and tests of endurance.
tell: Whether the muscle tires faster than the other side, and after how much activity.
Pain that comes with fatigue, and weakness or loss of power.
Trouble with coordination or control (for example, pushing off, stairs, running).
How the injury happened, how long it took to be treated, and any surgery.

nerve.label: Nerves (radiculopathy, neuropathy)
nerve.measured: Strength, reflexes, sensation, and how severe the nerve problem is (mild, moderate, severe).
tell: Exactly where you feel numbness, tingling, burning, or pain (which fingers or toes).
Weak grip, dropping things, or tripping, and how often.
Whether it is constant or comes and goes, and what brings it on.
Which hand you write with (your dominant side).

mental.label: Mental health (PTSD, depression, anxiety)
mental.measured: Your symptoms, how often they happen, and how much they affect work, family and social life.
tell: Your worst symptoms and how often they happen (nightmares, panic, anger, avoiding people, trouble concentrating).
Specific examples at work and at home: missed work, conflicts, pulling away from family, losing friends.
Your sleep: how many hours, how often you wake, nightmares.
Treatment and medicine, and whether they help.
If you have had thoughts of harming yourself, say so. If you are in crisis, call or text 988, then press 1.
extra: You don't have to describe traumatic events in detail. You can say 'it's in my records' or 'I'd rather not go into detail'.
Some Veterans bring a spouse or friend to wait outside. Ask the exam office about their rules.

tbi.label: Traumatic brain injury (TBI)
tbi.measured: Ten areas: memory and attention, judgment, social behavior, orientation, motor activity, visual-spatial skills, subjective symptoms, behavior, communication, and consciousness.
tell: Memory or attention problems, with real examples (missed appointments, losing track at work).
Headaches, dizziness, light or sound sensitivity, ringing, sleep problems.
Each blast or head injury you remember: when, where, and what you felt right after.
If you have memory complaints, ask whether neuropsychological testing can be done; testing can show problems a short exam misses.

headache.label: Migraines and headaches
headache.measured: How often you have prostrating attacks over the last several months, and how long they last.
tell: VA's word 'prostrating' means an attack so bad you can't carry on with ordinary activities: you have to stop, lie down or rest. Tell the examiner how often that happens, counting the last few months.
How long attacks last, and what you do during one (dark room, medicine, leave work).
Missed work or leaving early because of headaches, with dates if you have them.
Bring your headache log; it is the best evidence of how often attacks happen.

apnea.label: Sleep apnea
apnea.measured: Your sleep study result and the treatment you need (for example, a CPAP machine).
tell: Whether a provider prescribed a CPAP or other breathing machine, and how often you use it.
Daytime sleepiness: dozing off, trouble staying awake at work or driving.
extra: Bring the CPAP prescription or equipment order, and a usage report if your machine makes one.

hearing.label: Tinnitus and hearing
hearing.measured: A hearing test, and whether the ringing is recurrent.
tell: When the ringing started and what noise or blast it followed.
Whether it is constant or comes and goes, and how it affects sleep and conversations.

digestive.label: GERD and digestive conditions
digestive.measured: Symptoms, how often they happen, medicines you need, and any narrowing (stricture) found on tests.
tell: How many days a week you have symptoms, and whether you need medicine daily.
Trouble swallowing, food getting stuck, vomiting, or weight loss.
Any scope or swallow test you've had (bring the report).

skin.label: Scars
skin.measured: The number, size and location of each scar, and whether any is painful or unstable (breaks down).
tell: Show every scar, including small ones from scopes or stitches.
Any scar that hurts, itches, or breaks open, and how often.
Anything a scar keeps you from doing.

general.label: Other conditions
general.measured: What the condition is, how severe it is, and how it affects you.
tell: How often symptoms happen, how long they last, and what you can't do because of them.
